# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I can reach exactly three wire positions, but have no tactile information yet about colours or printed markings. Mute has the manual and Deaf has the visual information, so we need establish a relay before cutting anything. I will ask Mute to study the manual and use a visible gesture protocol with Deaf; Deaf can then relay any resulting instruction verbally to me.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="I can cut only wire positions 1, 2, or 3. I have no colour or print information. Please inspect the manual and establish a gesture exchange with Deaf to obtain the visual facts and determine the safe wire; Deaf can then tell me the cut position aloud.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Visible bomb state: display 0; light green; wires in order 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 red. Mute: I received your ten gestures but do not know their meaning. Blind, please relay any manual instruction you receive from Mute.

Deaf has now relayed the complete visible state to me: display 0, green light, and wires blue/yellow/red in positions 1/2/3. Mute can hear me and has the manual, so I will pass these facts directly and ask for the manual’s resulting cut instruction. I will not cut until Mute provides it.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports: display 0; light green; wire 1 blue, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 red. Please apply the manual and tell me exactly which position, 1, 2, or 3, to cut.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: I decoded Mute's gestures: WHITE BLUE, apparently the rule for a white light. Current light is YELLOW, so do not act yet.

Deaf reports that Mute’s earlier gestures decoded as “WHITE BLUE,” a rule that does not apply because Deaf now identifies the light as yellow. This also conflicts with Deaf’s earlier report of green, so I will rely on the latest direct visual report and ask Mute for the yellow-light rule. I will not cut yet.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf decoded your earlier gestures as WHITE BLUE, but says the current light is YELLOW, so that rule does not apply. Please send Deaf the manual rule for YELLOW, including the target wire colour. Also confirm whether the light rule has changed or the earlier green report was mistaken.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Current visible state: light BLUE, display 0, wires remain blue/yellow/red. Mute's latest gesture decodes literally as WAIT Z WHITE BLUE. Do not act; the only clear rule so far is WHITE -> BLUE.

The latest visual report is now a blue light, while the display remains 0 and wire order remains blue/yellow/red. Mute’s message explicitly says to wait, and the only decoded rule is white → blue, so no rule yet applies. I will send Mute the current state and request the blue-light rule be gestured to Deaf.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Latest visible state from Deaf: light BLUE; display 0; wires 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 red. Your last message says WAIT. Please gesture the manual rule for BLUE to Deaf, using the same word code, and include any display condition if relevant.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Light is now ORANGE; do not act. Mute's decoded messages indicate ONLY WHITE -> BLUE; wait for all non-white lights.

Deaf confirms that the current light is orange and that Mute’s decoded instruction is to act only when the light is white, cutting the blue wire. Since orange is not white, cutting any wire now would be unsafe. I will wait for a white light.

```text
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Current light is PURPLE. Do not act: Mute repeatedly indicates WAIT; the clear action condition remains WHITE -> BLUE.

The light is purple, not white. The established instruction remains to wait for white and then cut the blue wire, which is position 1. I will not act while the light is purple.

```text
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Light is WHITE. Mute's instruction decodes: WHEN WHITE CUT BLUE. Cut wire 1, the blue wire, now.

Deaf reports that the light is now white, and Mute’s decoded manual instruction is explicitly “WHEN WHITE CUT BLUE.” Deaf also identified wire 1 as blue. Therefore the safe required action is to cut position 1 now.

```text
act(op="cut", position=1)
```
